items.q: Is TiDB a drop-in replacement for MySQL / Aurora MySQL?
items.a: TiDB is MySQL-compatible—most applications connect with no code change. We recommend validating specifics in a proof-of-concept on your own schema to ensure compatibility with your workload.

items.q: How does TiDB scale past Aurora's limits?
items.a: TiDB scales reads and writes horizontally across nodes with no single-writer instance ceiling, while maintaining strong consistency. Add nodes to increase capacity without downtime or architectural changes.

items.q: Can one system really do OLTP and analytics?
items.a: Yes—TiFlash keeps columnar replicas synchronized with row-based storage, and the optimizer routes analytical queries to them on fresh data with no ETL. This hybrid architecture (HTAP) eliminates the need for separate analytics systems.

items.q: How do online schema changes work?
items.a: Online DDL runs in production without maintenance windows or blocking migrations. Schema changes are applied incrementally across the distributed system, allowing your application to continue serving traffic throughout the process.
